sounds.intro: Thai has five tones: mid, low, falling, high and rising. The same syllable changes meaning with the tone. Here the tones are not marked, so listen to a native speaker. The Latin line follows the Royal Thai General System, which is simple but ignores tones.
rows: breathy "k", "t", "p", with a puff of air
like "ng" in "singer", also at the start of a word
notes: Thai has no spaces between words. Spaces mark the end of a phrase or sentence.
Men end polite sentences with "khrap" (ครับ) and women with "kha" (ค่ะ) or "kha?" (คะ) for questions.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Thai has many pronouns, and the choice shows politeness and gender. Men say "phom" for I and women say "dichan" (formal) or "chan" (informal). Friends often use their names instead.
ex: ฉันเป็นนักเรียน
thoe pen phi sao khong chan
tur pen pee sow kong CHAN

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Thai nouns do not change for the plural. Context or a number shows how many. With a number, a classifier word goes between the number and the noun, such as "lem" for books.

grammar.title: To be: pen, khue, yu

text: Add "mai" at the end for a yes or no question. Reply by repeating the verb: "pai mai?" (go?) "pai" (go). Or add "chai mai" (right?).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Politeness is shown by the ending: men add "khrap", women add "kha". Using "khun" and "than" is more respectful. With friends, drop the particle.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: No verb changes. Past: add "laeo" (already) at the end. Future: put "cha" before the verb.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the bare verb. Add "noi" (a little) or "doi" to make it softer. To forbid, put "yaa" (do not) in front.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: "Dai" (can), "tong" (must) and "yak" (want) go before the main verb, or "dai" can go after it. "Mai dai" means cannot.

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Thai uses little words before the place: "thi" (at), "nai" (in), "bon" (on), "tai" (under), "kai" (near). Put them in front of the noun.
rows: ที่โรงเรียน
ex: the book is on the table
หนังสืออยู่บนโต๊ะ

ฉันอยู่ที่โรงเรียน

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "kwa" (more than) after the adjective: yai kwa (bigger than). For "the most", add "thi sut" (that is the end): yai thi sut.
rows: ใหญ่ ใหญ่กว่า
ดี ดีกว่า
ใหญ่ที่สุด
